body_en: Grand jury declines to indict ex-White House staffer who testified about January 6 | US Capitol attack
Grand jury declines to indict ex-White House staffer who testified about January 6
Cassidy Hutchinson had implicated Donald Trump in US Capitol attack during testimony before House committee

The justice department on Tuesday failed to secure a grand jury indictment against a former White House staffer who provided dramatic but disputed testimony against Donald Trump before a House committee investigating the 6 January 2021 US Capitol insurrection , according to two people familiar with the matter.

A grand jury in Washington rejected prosecutors’ request to return an indictment charging Cassidy Hutchinson , said the people, who spoke to the Associated Press on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to publicly discuss the case. It’s the latest setback in the justice department’s efforts to charge perceived adversaries of the Republican president.

Details of prosecutors’ allegations against Hutchinson were not immediately clear, but Republican lawmakers had accused her of lying under oath in her explosive testimony in 2022 about Trump’s behavior on January 6, when a mob of his supporters stormed the Capitol to halt the congressional certification of his election loss to Democrat Joe Biden.
‘You make me want to throw up’: Republicans attack ex-special counsel Jack Smith at Senate hearing

The account, at a surprise hearing announced just 24 hours earlier, was seen at the time as particularly powerful given Hutchinson’s proximity to power as special assistant to Mark Meadows, Trump’s chief of staff.

Hutchinson described an angry, defiant president who was trying to let armed protesters avoid security screenings at a rally that morning to protest his 2020 election defeat and who later grabbed at the steering wheel of the presidential SUV when the Secret Service refused to let him go to the Capitol. And when the events at the Capitol spiraled toward violence, with the crowd chanting “Hang Mike Pence”, she testified, Trump declined to intervene.
Trump at the time denied much of what Hutchinson said on his social media platform, Truth Social. He called her a “total phony” and “bad news”.

Hutchinson has alleged that members of Trump’s inner circle dangled job opportunities and financial assistance while she was cooperating with the committee. She also testified that her own lawyer – a former ethics counsel in the Trump White House – told her: “The less you remember, the better.”

The US House of Representatives impeached Trump in 2021 on allegations that he incited the mob that attacked the Capitol, but he was later acquitted by the Senate. The justice department under Biden charged Trump with felony offenses, accusing him of illegally working to overturn his 2020 election loss in the run-up to the Capitol attack, but then special counsel Jack Smith abandoned the case after Trump’s 2024 presidential victory. Longstanding justice department policy says sitting presidents cannot face criminal prosecution.

Hutchinson, a native of Pennington, New Jersey, previously worked in the White House office of legislative affairs and interned for Republicans, including the representative Steve Scalise of Louisiana and the senator Ted Cruz of Texas.

大陪审团拒绝起诉 1 月 6 日左右作证的前白宫工作人员
卡西迪·哈钦森在众议院委员会作证时暗示唐纳德·特朗普参与了美国国会大厦袭击事件
据两位知情人士透露，司法部周二未能让大陪审团对一名前白宫工作人员提出起诉，该工作人员在调查 2021 年 1 月 6 日美国国会大厦叛乱的众议院委员会上提供了针对唐纳德·特朗普的戏剧性但有争议的证词。
这些知情人士对美联社表示，华盛顿的一个大陪审团拒绝了检察官退回对卡西迪·哈钦森提出指控的起诉书的请求。这些人士要求匿名，因为他们无权公开讨论此案。这是司法部起诉共和党总统的对手的最新挫折。
检察官对哈钦森指控的细节尚不清楚，但共和党议员指责她在 2022 年针对特朗普 1 月 6 日行为的爆炸性证词中在宣誓后撒谎，当时特朗普的一群支持者冲进国会大厦，阻止国会认证他在选举中输给民主党人乔·拜登。
“你让我想呕吐”：共和党人在参议院听证会上攻击前特别顾问杰克·史密斯
就在 24 小时前的一次意外听证会上，这一说法在当时被认为特别有影响力，因为哈钦森作为特朗普幕僚长马克·梅多斯 (Mark Meadows) 的特别助理，与权力关系密切。
哈钦森描述了一位愤怒、目中无人的总统，当天早上，他在一场抗议 2020 年选举失败的集会上试图让武装抗议者避开安全检查，后来当特勤局拒绝让他前往国会大厦时，他抓住了总统 SUV 的方向盘。她作证说，当国会大厦的事件升级为暴力，人群高呼“绞死迈克·彭斯”时，特朗普拒绝干预。
特朗普当时否认了哈钦森在其社交媒体平台“Truth Social”上所说的大部分内容。他称她为“彻头彻尾的骗子”和“坏消息”。
哈钦森声称，在她与委员会合作期间，特朗普核心圈子的成员以就业机会和经济援助为条件。她还作证说，她自己的律师——特朗普白宫的前道德顾问——告诉她：“你记得的越少越好。”
美国众议院于2021年弹劾特朗普，指控他煽动暴徒袭击国会大厦，但后来被参议院宣告无罪。拜登领导下的司法部指控特朗普犯有重罪，指控他在国会大厦袭击前夕非法努力推翻自己在 2020 年选举中的失利，但特别检察官杰克·史密斯在特朗普 2024 年总统获胜后放弃了此案。司法部的长期政策规定，现任总统不能面临刑事起诉。
哈钦森是新泽西州彭宁顿人，此前曾在白宫立法事务办公室工作，并为共和党人实习，其中包括路易斯安那州众议员史蒂夫·斯卡利斯和德克萨斯州参议员特德·克鲁兹。

title_en: How congressional Democrats are preparing for claims of election fraud by Trump
title_zh: 国会民主党人如何准备应对特朗普的选举舞弊指控
summary: Democrats in Congress are bracing for what they fear could be meddling by President Trump or his allies with the results of this year's midterm elections.
summary_zh: 国会中的民主党人正准备应对他们担心的特朗普总统或其盟友可能会干预今年中期选举结果的情况。
body_en: How congressional Democrats are preparing for claims of election fraud by Trump : NPR

How congressional Democrats are preparing for claims of election fraud by Trump Democrats in Congress are bracing for what they fear could be meddling by President Trump or his allies with the results of this year's midterm elections.
How congressional Democrats are preparing for claims of election fraud by Trump
Congressional Democrats are forming a task force to protect election results
Democrats in Congress are bracing for what they fear could be meddling by President Trump or his allies with the results of this year's midterm elections.
If Democrats should win Tuesday's voting, their next task will be securing the vote.

The Trump administration has used the federal government's power to highlight the president's constant claims of voter fraud. Today, a judge hears arguments over the administration's effort to force California to set aside some ballots. The administration wants that treatment for people it claims are likely not citizens. An appeals court last night declined to get involved in that case.
INSKEEP: NPR congressional reporter Eric McDaniel is here in Studio 31 to give us an update on how Democrats are preparing to respond to all this. Eric, good morning.
ERIC MCDANIEL, BYLINE: Good morning. Good morning.
INSKEEP: OK. What do the preparations look like?

MCDANIEL: Well, I'll just say, for Democrats and this constellation of good governance and nonpartisan groups, the election disruption effort is ongoing, right? They point to things like a million-dollar bounty offered by President Trump yesterday for election fraud tips that lead to a conviction, though it's unclear how or if that would be paid. Department of Justice lawsuits in Alaska and California, like you mentioned. The failed effort by the administration to restrict mail-in voting. It's all been the subject of legal fights and will be.

Next, these folks are worried about things like a federal election emergency declaration, which is something that doesn't exist in law - troops at the polls, illegal - or the president saying, without providing any evidence, that a foreign enemy has hacked voting machines. So they've been trying to link up with local election officials, pre-write legal filings and get all of their talking points ready to go out and say the truth, which is that people should feel comfortable casting their ballots.

INSKEEP: OK. Understand that. You just mentioned a number of things that the president might say or do that would be illegal if he said or did them. What is the pattern about how the president talks about elections?

MCDANIEL: Well, I mean, I think you've mentioned this. The president's claimed fraud in every election he's been involved with. Just for the benefit of folks who are too young to remember. In 2016, Trump said he'd won the popular vote - he just won the Electoral College - when you discount millions of illegal votes. In 2018, he claimed there was electoral fraud in states like Arizona. The January 6 insurrection was about fraud claims in the 2020 presidential election. He told CNN that there was rigging going on in 2024.

It goes on and on. Last week, I talked to Representative Jim Himes. He's a Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, the ranking member there. He reminded me that he was actually in the Capitol during the January 6 insurrection and said it would be irresponsible for him and other Democrats not to be ready to combat fraud efforts.

INSKEEP: And I guess we should just mention once again, even the president's allies have never been able to substantiate the various claims of voter fraud in 2020 and other elections. But how does the White House describe what it's doing this time around?

MCDANIEL: Well, they say all of their work is to secure elections, which I should point out election experts say is already secure. Folks trust elections and election officials. I spent a good amount of time, though, this year reporting on the effort to get the SAVE America Act passed, which the White House claimed would protect the election by restricting mail-in voting and requiring folks to show proof of their citizenship status in order to stay registered to vote. It failed due to a lack of Republican support in the Senate. Earlier this month, a reporter actually pressed the president on if he would honor the results. Listen to this.
PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: What do you think the answer is to that?
UNIDENTIFIED REPORTER: I don't know, Mr. President.
TRUMP: Of course I will. But we don't want cheating.
body_zh: 国会民主党人如何准备应对特朗普的选举舞弊指控：NPR
国会民主党人如何准备应对特朗普的选举舞弊指控 国会中的民主党人正在为他们担心的特朗普总统或其盟友可能干预今年中期选举的结果做好准备。
国会民主党人如何准备应对特朗普的选举舞弊指控
国会民主党人正在组建一个特别工作组来保护选举结果
国会中的民主党人正准备应对他们担心的特朗普总统或其盟友可能会干预今年中期选举结果的情况。
如果民主党赢得周二的投票，他们的下一个任务将是确保选票。
特朗普政府利用联邦政府的权力来强调总统不断声称的选民欺诈行为。今天，一名法官听取了有关政府试图迫使加州搁置部分选票的争论。政府希望对其声称的可能不是公民的人进行这种待遇。上诉法院昨晚拒绝介入该案。
因斯基普：NPR 国会记者埃里克·麦克丹尼尔 (Eric McDaniel) 在 31 工作室向我们介绍民主党准备如何应对这一切的最新情况。埃里克，早上好。
埃里克·麦克丹尼尔连线：早上好。早上好。
因斯基普：好的。准备工作是什么样的？
麦克丹尼尔：嗯，我只想说，对于民主党以及这个由良好治理和无党派团体组成的群体来说，破坏选举的努力正在进行中，对吧？他们指出，特朗普总统昨天为导致定罪的选举舞弊举报提供了百万美元的赏金，尽管目前还不清楚如何或是否支付这笔奖金。正如您提到的，司法部在阿拉斯加和加利福尼亚州提起诉讼。政府限制邮寄投票的努力失败了。这一切一直都是法律斗争的主题，而且将来也会如此。
接下来，这些人担心诸如联邦选举紧急声明之类的事情，这是法律中不存在的事情——军队参加投票站，是非法的——或者总统在没有提供任何证据的情况下说外敌入侵了投票机。因此，他们一直在努力与当地选举官员联系，预先编写法律文件，并准备好所有谈话要点，以便说出真相，即人们应该放心地投票。
因斯基普：好的。明白这一点。你刚才提到了总统可能说或做的一些事情，如果他说或做了这些事情就是非法的。总统谈论选举的模式是什么？
麦克丹尼尔：嗯，我的意思是，我想你已经提到过这一点。总统声称他参与的每一次选举都存在舞弊行为。只是为了那些太年轻而不记得的人的利益。 2016年，特朗普表示，当你扣除数百万张非法选票时，他赢得了普选——他刚刚赢得了选举人团。 2018年，他声称亚利桑那州等州存在选举舞弊行为。 1 月 6 日的叛乱与 2020 年总统选举中的舞弊指控有关。他告诉 CNN，2024 年存在操纵行为。
它一直持续着。上周，我与众议员吉姆·希姆斯进行了交谈。他是众议院情报委员会的民主党人，是该委员会的高级成员。他提醒我，1 月 6 日的叛乱期间他实际上就在国会大厦，并表示如果他和其他民主党人不做好打击欺诈行为的准备，那将是不负责任的行为。
因斯基普：我想我们应该再次提及，即使是总统的盟友也从未能够证实 2020 年和其他选举中选民欺诈的各种说法。但白宫如何描述这次的行动呢？
麦克丹尼尔：嗯，他们说他们所有的工作都是为了确保选举的安全，我应该指出，选举专家说选举已经是安全的。人们信任选举和选举官员。不过，今年我花了很多时间报道《拯救美国法案》通过的努力，白宫声称该法案将通过限制邮寄投票并要求人们出示公民身份证明以保持登记投票来保护选举。由于参议院缺乏共和党的支持，该计划失败了。本月早些时候，一名记者实际上向总统施压，询问他是否会遵守这一结果。听听这个。
唐纳德·特朗普总统：您认为答案是什么？
身份不明的记者：我不知道，总统先生。
特朗普：我当然会。但我们不想作弊。

body_en: Trump shows off tanker with ‘1m barrels of oil’ and floats Venezuela as 51st state | Donald Trump
Trump shows off tanker with ‘1m barrels of oil’ and floats Venezuela as 51st state
President at Texas campaign rally hails deal struck with post-Maduro government as ‘greatest oil victory in history’

Donald Trump suggested Venezuela become the 51st state of the United States on Tuesday as the president showed off a tanker he claimed had “one million barrels of oil on it” from the country, nine months after deposing its president.
At a campaign rally in Corpus Christ, Texas, Trump touted a US oil deal with Venezuela, which the US attacked in January, capturing its long-serving leader Nicolás Maduro .
Trump claims the agreement – struck with the South American country’s interim government , which is backed by Trump’s administration – will cover “billions” of barrels of oil.
Venezuela “will become a prosperous country, and who knows? Maybe some day soon it’ll become a prosperous 51st state,” Trump said at the podium on Tuesday. “That’s possible.”
Venezuela is on a growing list of countries and territories Trump has spoken of acquiring, including Greenland, Canada and Mexico.

With tens of millions of Americans set to vote in next week’s midterm elections, Trump’s aggressive foreign policy – including his controversial war on Iran, and tariffs on goods from much of the world – have challenged his popularity, according to opinion polls, with his approval ratings falling to record lows.

But on Tuesday, the president sought to point to the Venezuela operation as an example of his success. US fuel prices, which surged after the start of the Iran war, piling pressure on Americans’ cost of living, “will soon come plummeting down”, he claimed in a social media post.

“We’re celebrating the greatest oil victory in history,” he said at the rally, pointing out the ship off the Texan coast. “The oil provided is being provided to the United States at zero cost to the American taxpayer.”

Moments before Trump took the stage in Texas, he claimed on his Truth Social platform: “By unleashing Energy Dominance from Alaska, all the way down to Venezuela, I have made the Western Hemisphere the Energy Capital of the World.”

The deal has also drawn skepticism as critics complained that the Trump administration has not pushed a transition to democracy in Venezuela, were elections have not been held since Maduro was detained by US forces and taken to New York to face criminal charges after a raid on his Caracas residence.

The urgency of the oil agreement stems from Trump’s opting into the war with Iran in February. Gas prices have shot up nationwide after Iran closed the strait of Hormuz, a passageway for 20% of the world’s oil supplies.

特朗普炫耀拥有“100万桶石油”的油轮并将委内瑞拉列为第51个国家
德克萨斯州竞选集会上的总统称赞与后马杜罗政府达成的协议是“历史上最伟大的石油胜利”
唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 周二建议委内瑞拉成为美国第 51 个州，在罢免总统九个月后，总统展示了一艘他声称船上“装有 100 万桶石油”的油轮。
在得克萨斯州科珀斯基督市的一次竞选集会上，特朗普宣扬了美国与委内瑞拉的一项石油协议，美国在一月份攻击了委内瑞拉，俘获了长期任职的领导人尼古拉斯·马杜罗。
特朗普声称，与特朗普政府支持的南美国家临时政府达成的协议将涵盖“数十亿”桶石油。
特朗普周二在讲台上表示，委内瑞拉“将成为一个繁荣的国家，谁知道呢？也许很快有一天它就会成为第 51 个繁荣的国家”。 “有可能。”
委内瑞拉是特朗普谈到的越来越多的国家和领土之一，其中包括格陵兰岛、加拿大和墨西哥。
民意调查显示，随着数千万美国人即将在下周的中期选举中投票，特朗普激进的外交政策 — — 包括备受争议的伊朗战争以及对世界大部分地区的商品征收关税 — — 对他的支持率构成了挑战，他的支持率跌至历史最低点。
但周二，总统试图以委内瑞拉行动作为他成功的例子。他在社交媒体帖子中声称，伊朗战争爆发后美国燃油价格飙升，给美国人的生活成本带来了压力，“很快就会大幅下降”。
“我们正在庆祝历史上最伟大的石油胜利，”他在集会上指着德克萨斯海岸附近的这艘船说道。 “所提供的石油是以美国纳税人零成本提供给美国的。”
特朗普在德克萨斯州登台演讲前不久，他在自己的“真相社交”平台上宣称：“通过释放从阿拉斯加一直到委内瑞拉的能源主导地位，我已经使西半球成为世界能源之都。”
该协议也引发了质疑，因为批评者抱怨说，自从马杜罗在加拉加斯住所遭到袭击后被美军拘留并带到纽约面临刑事指控以来，委内瑞拉就没有举行选举，因此特朗普政府没有推动委内瑞拉向民主过渡。
石油协议的紧迫性源于特朗普二月份选择与伊朗开战。伊朗关闭霍尔木兹海峡后，全国天然气价格飙升，霍尔木兹海峡是全球 20% 石油供应的通道。

title_en: Republicans wanted Rubio on the stump. Trump coaxed him there.
title_zh: 共和党人希望卢比奥上台。特朗普把他哄到了那里。
summary: “We love you, Texas,” the secretary of State told the crowd.
summary_zh: “我们爱你，德克萨斯州，”国务卿对人群说。
body_en: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday came as close to the campaign trail as he’s been all year. And even then, he tried to stay just offshore.

Rubio appeared with President Donald Trump in Corpus Christi, Texas, as he rallied alongside an oil tanker carrying Venezuelan crude. The visit helped spotlight a proud White House accomplishment — toppling the Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro and opening the country’s energy supply — in a political battleground state.

The unexpected nature of Rubio’s presence, after the president coaxed him up on stage during the rally, is likely enough to shield the nation’s top diplomat from allegations that he is interfering in the midterm campaign. The former Florida senator has kept a careful distance from partisan politics, even as colleagues like Attorney General Todd Blanche have defied longstanding norms against some administration officials engaging in electioneering.

“It's an honor to work for the greatest country in the world, for the greatest president in the history of the United States of America,” Rubio said in brief remarks from the stage. “We love you, Texas.”

A White House official, who like others in this article was granted anonymity to share details of the trip, said that Rubio was backstage during the rally when the president brought him up and that he was only there in his capacity as national security adviser, not to stump ahead of the midterms.

While Rubio, who was not expected to speak at the event, has maintained the tradition of secretaries of State not campaigning, Republicans have been clamoring for the potential 2028 presidential hopeful to do so, seeing him as one of the party’s strongest messengers in a bruising midterm cycle in which they have been desperate for any additional help. One GOP official in a state with a key Senate race, granted anonymity to share private conversations, said that they asked for Rubio to attend a recent political event but were told the secretary of State wasn't doing political events given his role as chief diplomatic officer.

“Rubio is Trump’s best asset, and they know they are in a dog fight to win in Texas,” said Bill Cortese, a GOP operative who has advised Rep. Elise Stefanik (R-N.Y.). Even if Rubio had not come up on stage, “news of Rubio simply being in the state could potentially boost the GOP’s chances in places that they need it.”

Plus, the secretary of State had another good reason for being there: Rubio was one of the central architects of the administration’s Venezuela strategy and has been a leading figure in managing the country’s political transition and economic arrangements with the U.S. in the wake of Maduro’s ouster.
“It’s his win and his deal,” a Trump administration official added about Rubio and the Venezuela link.

Asked why Rubio accompanied Trump on the Texas trip, the White House referred to one of Trump’s Truth Social posts from August in which he credited Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth for negotiating the oil deal with Venezuela.

A State Department spokesperson noted Rubio’s role as national security adviser and said that he “needs time with the president on all kinds of issues. The president will be on the go, so being on the plane with him gives him a chance to talk to him about these items.”
The secretary of State notably skipped the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention in Dallas last month, opting instead to go on a diplomatic trip to Colombia.

“Marco loves campaigns and politics and he cares desperately about making sure that the House and Senate remain in Republican hands, but I think he also realizes that part of being secretary of State is you don’t engage in overt political activity,” said a person close to Rubio.

In Trump’s first term, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo broke with tradition and made a handful of public appearances that directly or indirectly appeared campaign related, including delivering remarks to the Republican National Convention in 2020.

On a practical level, most secretaries of State travel overseas so much that it’s hard to spare time for campaigns. But Rubio travels more infrequently than his predecessors, in part because of his national security adviser role, which keeps him at the White House.

And Rubio also has a more nontraditional role even as secretary of State, focusing most of his energy on Latin America while the president’s special envoys, including Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, have handled negotiations to try to end the wars in Iran, Ukraine and Gaza.

Yet the Texas visit — in which Trump sought to link one of his signature foreign policy accomplishments with efforts to reduce prices — came as a relief to the Republicans who believe Rubio is one of the party’s most trusted messengers on the economy and have for months wanted to see him on the trail.

Results from The POLITICO Poll suggest Rubio can be a useful surrogate on the campaign trail. Across three polls this month, Republican midterm voters consistently selected Rubio as their third-highest choice to hit the campaign trail to help their party, behind Trump and Vice President JD Vance but ahead of Texas Sen. Ted Cruz, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and others.

Support for Rubio on the campaign trail is also fairly steady across Trump’s 2024 coalition, with only an 8-point gap between the MAGA base (31%) and non-MAGA Trump voters (23%) saying the secretary of State would help Republicans if he campaigned. Meanwhile, MAGA loyalists were significantly more likely than non-MAGA Trump voters to support Trump and Vance hitting the trail.

Notably, Rubio also generates less negative backlash than other figures. Democrats widely support the impeachment of Trump, Vance, Kennedy and others. But support for impeaching Rubio is lower than the other figures, pushing overall public opinion against impeachment.
body_zh: 国务卿马可·卢比奥周二接近竞选活动，这是他全年以来最接近的一次。即便如此，他还是试图留在离岸地区。
卢比奥与唐纳德·特朗普总统一起出现在德克萨斯州科珀斯克里斯蒂，当时他在一艘运载委内瑞拉原油的油轮旁边集会。这次访问凸显了白宫在这个政治战场国家取得的令人自豪的成就——推翻委内瑞拉独裁者尼古拉斯·马杜罗并开放该国的能源供应。
在总统在集会期间将卢比奥哄上台后，卢比奥的出人意料的出现可能足以使该国最高外交官免受有关他干涉中期选举的指控。这位前佛罗里达州参议员一直与党派政治保持着谨慎的距离，尽管司法部长托德·布兰奇等同事违反了长期以来反对一些​​政府官员参与竞选的规范。
“为世界上最伟大的国家、为美利坚合众国历史上最伟大的总统工作是我的荣幸，”卢比奥在台上发表简短讲话时说道。 “我们爱你，德克萨斯。”
一位与本文中的其他人一样被要求匿名分享此行细节的白宫官员表示，总统在集会期间提到卢比奥时，他正在后台，他只是以国家安全顾问的身份出现在后台，而不是为了在中期选举前作秀。
虽然预计不会在活动中发言的卢比奥保持了国务卿不竞选的传统，但共和党人一直呼吁有望在 2028 年当选的总统发言，认为他是该党在艰难的中期周期中最强大的使者之一，在这个周期中，他们迫切需要任何额外的帮助。参议院竞选关键州的一名不愿透露姓名的共和党官员表示，他们要求卢比奥参加最近的一次政治活动，但被告知，鉴于国务卿担任首席外交官，他不会参加政治活动。
“卢比奥是特朗普最好的资产，他们知道他们正在为赢得德克萨斯州而进行一场恶战，”为纽约州共和党众议员埃莉斯·斯特凡尼克提供咨询的共和党特工比尔·科特斯说。即使卢比奥没有上台，“卢比奥在该州的消息也可能会增加共和党在他们需要的地方的机会。”
此外，国务卿出席还有另一个充分的理由：卢比奥是政府委内瑞拉战略的核心设计师之一，并且在马杜罗下台后一直是管理该国政治过渡和与美国的经济安排的领军人物。
“这是他的胜利和他的协议，”特朗普政府官员在谈到卢比奥和委内瑞拉的联系时补充道。
当被问及卢比奥为何陪同特朗普前往德克萨斯州时，白宫提到了特朗普八月份在《真相社会》上发布的一篇帖子，其中他称赞卢比奥和国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯在与委内瑞拉的石油协议谈判中做出了贡献。
美国国务院发言人提到了卢比奥作为国家安全顾问的角色，并表示他“需要与总统就各种问题进行交流。总统会经常出差，因此与他一起乘坐飞机让他有机会与总统讨论这些问题。”
国务卿特别缺席了上个月在达拉斯举行的共和党全国委员会中期大会，而是选择对哥伦比亚进行外交访问。
“马可热爱竞选和政治，他非常关心确保众议院和参议院仍掌握在共和党手中，但我认为他也意识到，担任国务卿的一部分就是不要参与公开的政治活动，”一位与卢比奥关系密切的人士表示。
在特朗普的第一个任期内，国务卿迈克·蓬佩奥 (Mike Pompeo) 打破传统，进行了几次直接或间接与竞选相关的公开露面，包括在 2020 年共和党全国代表大会上发表讲话。
实际上，大多数国务卿经常出国，很难抽出时间参加竞选活动。但卢比奥的出行频率比他的前任要少，部分原因是他的国家安全顾问角色使他留在了白宫。
即使担任国务卿，卢比奥也扮演着更非传统的角色，他将大部分精力集中在拉丁美洲，而包括史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳在内的总统特使则负责处理旨在结束伊朗、乌克兰和加沙战争的谈判。
然而，特朗普试图将其标志性外交政策成就之一与降低物价的努力联系起来的德克萨斯州之行，让共和党人松了一口气，他们认为卢比奥是该党最值得信赖的经济使者之一，几个月来一直希望看到他的身影。
POLITICO 民意调查的结果表明卢比奥可以成为竞选活动中的有用代理人。在本月的三项民意调查中，共和党中期选民一致选择卢比奥作为他们在竞选活动中帮助本党的第三大选择，仅次于特朗普和副总统万斯，但领先于德克萨斯州参议员特德·克鲁兹、卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪等人。
在特朗普的2024年联盟中，卢比奥在竞选过程中的支持率也相当稳定，支持MAGA的选民(31%)和非MAGA特朗普选民(23%)之间只有8个百分点的差距，他们认为国务卿如果参加竞选就会帮助共和党。与此同时，“MAGA”的忠实拥护者比非“MAGA”特朗普选民更有可能支持特朗普和万斯继续前进。
值得注意的是，与其他人物相比，卢比奥产生的负面反应也较少。民主党广泛支持弹劾特朗普、万斯、肯尼迪等人。但弹劾卢比奥的支持率低于其他数字，推动整体民意反对弹劾。

title_en: Grand jury declines to indict former Trump aide Cassidy Hutchinson, star witness of Jan. 6 committee
title_zh: 大陪审团拒绝起诉特朗普前助手、1月6日委员会的明星证人卡西迪·哈钦森
summary: The failed indictment is one of many for federal prosecutors during the second Trump administration.
summary_zh: 这次失败的起诉书是特朗普第二届政府期间联邦检察官提出的众多起诉书之一。
body_en: By Michael Kosnar , Ryan J. Reilly , Justin Goldman and Dareh Gregorian

A federal grand jury Tuesday declined to indict Cassidy Hutchinson — the former White House aide turned star witness against President Donald Trump — on criminal charges, a senior U.S. official confirmed to NBC News.
Prosecutors were attempting to indict Hutchinson for statements she made about Trump’s actions on Jan. 6, 2021.

The grand jury in Washington returned a “no bill,” meaning the grand jury rejected efforts by the Justice Department to indict Hutchinson. Her name was not mentioned in the courtroom when the no bill was announced, but the senior U.S. official confirmed it was the Hutchinson case.
Attorneys for Hutchinson did not immediately return requests for comment, nor did the Justice Department.
The Justice Department’s investigation had centered on Hutchinson’s 2022 testimony before the now-defunct Democratic-led congressional Jan. 6 committee, which Trump railed against for years.
The failure to secure an indictment is the latest in a string of such denials in cases the Justice Department has brought against those Trump has portrayed as his political enemies.

The Hutchinson case was brought by officials in the Civil Rights Division, which is headed by Trump appointee Harmeet Dhillon . The division has traditionally sought to protect constitutional freedoms by enforcing federal civil rights and anti-discrimination laws.
The grand jury’s refusal to indict Hutchinson does not bar the DOJ from attempting to charge her again in the future.
Trump has called Hutchinson a “scam artist” who lied under oath and has suggested she be prosecuted.

“What is the Justice Department going to do about this?” he wrote in a 2022 post on Truth Social. In March, he posted a link to a Breitbart article about House Republicans referring her to the Justice Department for prosecution.

Hutchinson, who’d been a senior aide to then-White House chief of staff Mark Meadows, made several damaging claims to the committee about Trump’s behavior in the days leading up to the Jan. 6, 2021, storming of the U.S. Capitol and during the riot itself.

Among the incidents she testified about were the president urging that metal detectors be removed from the area near the White House where he was speaking on Jan. 6. She quoted him as saying the rally attendees are “not here to hurt me,” and “I don’t f---ing care that they have weapons.”

Hutchinson also testified that the president was determined to go to the Capitol on Jan. 6, and that she’d been told by a Secret Service official that Trump grabbed for the steering wheel of the presidential limo — and the throat of one of his bodyguards — when the bodyguard refused to take him to the Capitol.
Secret Service officials later denied that account. Hutchinson has maintained that she provided truthful testimony.
A grand jury heard evidence against Hutchinson in early October, a person familiar with the effort told NBC News this month.

The Justice Department has been investigating and in some cases secured indictments of Trump’s perceived political enemies. Those who’ve been investigated or charged include Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif.; former CIA Director John Brennan; New York Attorney General Letitia James; and former FBI Director James Comey . Trump has accused all four of criminal wrongdoing, which they’ve denied.
After an initial case against James was dismissed on technical grounds, the Justice Department attempted to secure an indictment against her three separate times , all of which were denied.

The Trump administration also tried and failed to indict six sitting Democratic members of Congress over a social media video Trump disliked that told members of the military and intelligence communities not to obey unlawful orders.
Attorney General Todd Blanche told NBC News in April that the failed prosecutions showed “that we’re working hard.”
body_zh: 作者：Michael Kosnar、Ryan J. Reilly、Justin Goldman 和 Dareh Gregorian
一位美国高级官员向 NBC 新闻证实，周二，联邦大陪审团拒绝对前白宫助手、成为唐纳德·特朗普总统的明星证人卡西迪·哈钦森 (Cassidy Hutchinson) 提起刑事指控。
检察官正试图起诉哈钦森 2021 年 1 月 6 日就特朗普行为发表的言论。
华盛顿大陪审团返回了“否决法案”，这意味着大陪审团拒绝了司法部起诉哈钦森的努力。当宣布否决法案时，法庭上没有提到她的名字，但美国高级官员证实这是哈钦森案。
哈钦森的律师和司法部都没有立即回复置评请求。
司法部的调查集中在哈钦森 2022 年在民主党领导的国会 1 月 6 日委员会（现已解散）面前的证词，特朗普多年来一直对该委员会表示不满。
未能获得起诉是司法部针对特朗普描述为政敌的人提起的一系列此类否认案件中的最新一起。
哈钦森案是由民权部门的官员提起的，该部门由特朗普任命的哈米特·迪隆 (Harmeet Dhillon) 领导。该部门传统上寻求通过执行联邦公民权利和反歧视法来保护宪法自由。
大陪审团拒绝起诉哈钦森并不妨碍司法部将来再次尝试对她提出指控。
特朗普称哈钦森为“骗子”，她在宣誓后撒了谎，并建议起诉她。
“司法部对此将采取什么行动？”他在 2022 年发表在 Truth Social 上的一篇文章中写道。今年三月，他发布了一篇布赖特巴特新闻网文章的链接，内容是众议院共和党人将她移交给司法部起诉。
哈钦森曾担任时任白宫幕僚长马克·梅多斯 (Mark Meadows) 的高级助手，他就特朗普在 2021 年 1 月 6 日冲击美国国会大厦之前以及骚乱期间的行为向委员会提出了几项具有破坏性的指控。
在她作证的事件中，总统敦促将金属探测器从他 1 月 6 日发表讲话的白宫附近区域拆除。她引用总统的话说，集会参加者“不是来伤害我的”，“我他妈的才不在乎他们有武器”。
哈钦森还作证说，总统决心在 1 月 6 日前往国会大厦，一名特勤局官员告诉她，当保镖拒绝带他去国会大厦时，特朗普抓住了总统豪华轿车的方向盘，并掐住了他的一名保镖的喉咙。
特勤局官员后来否认了这一说法。哈钦森坚称她提供了真实的证词。
一位知情人士本月告诉 NBC 新闻，大陪审团于 10 月初听取了对哈钦森不利的证据。
司法部一直在调查，并在某些案件中对特朗普的政治敌人提出了起诉。受到调查或指控的人包括加利福尼亚州民主党参议员亚当·希夫 (Adam Schiff)；前中央情报局局长约翰·布伦南；纽约州总检察长利蒂西亚·詹姆斯；和前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米。特朗普指控这四人有刑事不当行为，但他们否认了这一点。
在针对詹姆斯的最初案件因技术原因被驳回后，司法部曾三次试图对她提出起诉，但均被拒绝。
特朗普政府还试图起诉六名现任民主党国会议员，原因是特朗普不喜欢一段社交媒体视频，该视频告诉军方和情报界成员不要服从非法命令。
司法部长托德·布兰奇 (Todd Blanche) 四月份告诉 NBC 新闻，失败的起诉表明“我们正在努力工作”。

title_en: New charges tossed against ex-FBI officials in Hunter Biden probe
title_zh: 亨特·拜登调查中对前联邦调查局官员提出新指控
summary: The unsigned and unsworn superseding complaint comes just hours before the defendants were due to appear in federal court in Washington, D.C. for a preliminary hearing.
summary_zh: 这份未经签署和宣誓的替代性起诉书是在被告将在华盛顿特区的联邦法院出庭接受诉讼前几个小时提出的。
body_en: Washington — A federal magistrate judge on Tuesday rejected the Justice Department's 11th-hour attempt to file new criminal charges against two former FBI counterintelligence officials accused of lying to Congress about their role in the Hunter Biden laptop probe.

During an often-tense hourslong court hearing, the FBI agent assigned to the investigation also acknowledged to a defense attorney that when he was put on the case over the summer, he was concerned it could be seen as "controversial" and "political."

Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia expressed shock and anger at the Justice Department for filing an unsworn and unsigned superseding complaint against the two FBI officials — Bradley Benavides and Nicole Floris — after midnight on Tuesday on the public court docket. Faruqui noted that it was never reviewed by him to establish whether there was probable cause a crime was committed.

Filing an unsworn complaint on the public docket and bypassing judicial review, he said, is unheard of and raises questions about the DOJ's motivations. He said he would be ordering that the new version of the charging documents be "struck from the record," though the Justice Department could try to add new charges the proper way.

The docket was later updated to say that the Justice Department's filings were entered "in error." The original criminal complaint, which was filed last week, is still intact, accusing Floris and Benavides of falsely suggesting to the House Judiciary Committee that they weren't aware of the government's investigations surrounding Hunter Biden.
Faruqui said, "We have never had complaints filed that are unsigned," calling it "inappropriate" and saying it "harms the defendants."
"I am unaware of that ever happening before in this court," he added. "I am frustrated that I got it in the middle of the night. But I am much more concerned that it is filed on the public record."

John Borchert, a prosecutor from the U.S. Attorney's Office in Washington, D.C., conceded that the effort by the government to add fresh charges without judicial review in a criminal complaint was a first for him as well.

He asked if Faruqui would agree to let the FBI agent who filed the affidavit in support of the new complaint swear and attest to his filing and then proceed with a hearing to determine if probable cause was met.
Defense attorneys for the two ex-officials balked, with one calling such a move "Kafkaesque" and Faruqui analogizing such an action to simply serving as a notary.

Faruqui accused the government of repeatedly making bizarre moves in the case that only raise concerns, saying it was like throwing gasoline on a fire, citing how the case was charged and the decision to use a special assistant U.S. attorney from out of town to help prosecute the case.

"Everything you're doing is making me more and more concerned," he said. "Why today on this one case have you changed the entire history of how you charge cases? It makes it look like the United States is afraid of me trying to find probable cause."
"Let me address that squarely. We are not afraid of a probable cause finding," Borchert said.

Faruqui said that while he was dismissing the superseding complaint with the new charge of obstructing a congressional proceeding, the court would still proceed with a preliminary hearing to determine whether the original criminal complaint charging them with lying to Congress , which was reviewed by a magistrate judge, meets the probable cause standard.

Mary Dohrmann, one of Floris' attorneys, told the court that the changes between the original complaint and the new one the government tried to file were substantial and raised concerns about accuracy.
"The evidence is mounting that this prosecution is about some political football, and not the law or the facts in this case," she said.

Criminal complaints in felony cases are typically reserved for more exigent circumstances, such as ongoing threats to public safety or national security. And Justice Department guidelines and norms have typically urged prosecutors to avoid taking overt investigative steps on politically sensitive cases so close to a national election.
Prosecutors filing an unsworn and unsigned superseding complaint overnight is likely to raise further questions about whether the case is politically motivated.

"What is going on at the D.C. U.S. Attorney's Office? In the middle of the night, the government filed an unsigned and unsworn complaint attempting to fix the issues with their original charge against Ms. Floris and adding a new charge just as meritless as the first one," said Floris' legal team in a statement provided to CBS News.
body_zh: 华盛顿——周二，一名联邦地方法官驳回了司法部在第 11 小时对两名前联邦调查局反情报官员提出新刑事指控的尝试，他们被控在亨特·拜登笔记本电脑调查中向国会撒谎。
在一场经常紧张的长达数小时的法庭听证会上，负责调查的联邦调查局特工还向一名辩护律师承认，当他在夏天接手此案时，他担心这可能会被视为“有争议的”和“政治性的”。
美国哥伦比亚特区地方法院治安法官齐亚·法鲁基 (Zia Faruqui) 对司法部于周二午夜后在公共法庭备审记录中对两名联邦调查局官员布拉德利·贝纳维德斯 (Bradley Benavides) 和妮可·弗洛里斯 (Nicole Floris) 提出未经宣誓和未签名的替代申诉表示震惊和愤怒。法鲁基指出，他从未审查过是否存在犯罪的可能原因。
他说，在公共备审案件中提出未经宣誓的申诉并绕过司法审查是闻所未闻的，这引发了人们对司法部动机的质疑。他表示，他将下令“从记录中删除”新版本的指控文件，尽管司法部可能会尝试以适当的方式添加新指控。
案卷后来更新称司法部的文件输入“错误”。上周提交的最初刑事起诉书仍然完好无损，指控弗洛里斯和贝纳维德斯向众议院司法委员会错误地暗示，他们不知道政府对亨特·拜登的调查。
法鲁基说，“我们从未收到过未经签署的投诉”，称其“不恰当”并称其“伤害了被告”。
“我不知道法庭上以前发生过这种事，”他补充道。 “我很沮丧，我在半夜收到了它。但我更担心它被记录在公共记录中。”
华盛顿特区美国检察官办公室的检察官约翰·博尔切特 (John Borchert) 承认，政府在刑事申诉中未经司法审查而增加新指控的做法对他来说也是第一次。
他询问法鲁基是否同意让提交宣誓书以支持新投诉的联邦调查局特工宣誓并证明他的文件，然后举行听证会以确定是否满足可能的理由。
两名前官员的辩护律师犹豫不决，其中一名律师称此举“卡夫卡式”，而法鲁基则将这种行为比作简单地充当公证人。
法鲁基指责政府在该案中一再采取怪异举动，只会引起担忧，称这就像火上浇油，并列举了该案的指控方式以及决定使用一名来自外地的特别助理美国检察官来帮助起诉该案。
“你所做的一切让我越来越担心，”他说。 “为什么今天在这一起案件上，你们改变了整个起诉方式的历史？这让美国看起来像是害怕我试图找到可能的原因。”
“让我直接解决这个问题。我们并不害怕找到可能的原因，”博尔切特说。
法鲁基表示，虽然他以阻碍国会诉讼的新指控驳回了替代指控，但法院仍将进行初步听证会，以确定指控他们向国会撒谎的最初刑事指控是否符合可能原因标准，该指控已由治安法官审查。
弗洛里斯的律师之一玛丽·多尔曼 (Mary Dohrmann) 告诉法庭，最初的申诉与政府试图提交的新申诉之间的变化很大，引发了人们对准确性的担忧。
“越来越多的证据表明，这次起诉是关于一些政治足球，而不是法律或本案的事实，”她说。
重罪案件中的刑事投诉通常是在更紧急的情况下提出的，例如对公共安全或国家安全的持续威胁。司法部的指导方针和规范通常敦促检察官避免对如此接近全国大选的政治敏感案件采取公开的调查措施。
检察官连夜提交未经宣誓和未签署的替代起诉书可能会引发有关此案是否出于政治动机的进一步质疑。
弗洛里斯的法律团队在向哥伦比亚广播公司新闻提供的一份声明中表示，“华盛顿特区美国检察官办公室发生了什么事？半夜，政府提交了一份未经签署和宣誓的起诉书，试图解决对弗洛里斯女士最初指控的问题，并增加了一项与第一项指控一样毫无根据的新指控。”

title_en: JD Vance steps up extreme attacks on Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed
title_zh: JD 万斯加大对民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的极端攻击力度
summary: Vice-president tries to link El-Sayed to Paris protests and claims he would lead rioters in ‘burning down’ Detroit JD Vance has escalated his inflammatory attacks on Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate for US Senate in Michigan who has faced an onslaught
summary_zh: 副总统试图将埃尔-赛义德与巴黎抗议活动联系起来，并声称他将领导骚乱者“烧毁”底特律 JD Vance 加剧了他的愤怒
body_en: JD Vance steps up extreme attacks on Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed | US midterm elections 2026
JD Vance steps up extreme attacks on Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed
Vice-president tries to link El-Sayed to Paris protests and claims he would lead rioters in ‘burning down’ Detroit

JD Vance has escalated his inflammatory attacks on Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate for US Senate in Michigan who has faced an onslaught of Islamophobia, claiming he would lead rioters in “burning down” Detroit.
El-Sayed, who would become the country’s first Muslim senator if he wins next week’s election, has been branded a “jihadist” by Donald Trump , the US president.

Vance, the vice-president, has already alleged El-Sayed was a representative of “terrible evil” who fights for “one group at the expense of others” – prompting El-Sayed to respond it was “evil” to deprive people of healthcare and affordable groceries.
At a campaign stop on Tuesday, Vance went further.

Speaking to the crowd in Howell, Michigan, Vance sought to connect El-Sayed’s politics to the leftwing protests in Paris that have led to thousands of arrests. Describing “hordes of masked rioters, many from distant lands, taking over historic city centers”, the vice-president also played up El-Sayed’s relationship with leftwing political commentator Hasan Piker .

“The scene of destruction in Paris may be an ocean away, but ask yourselves: are they really so hard to imagine here in the United States of America?” Vance said. “And I guarantee you, if those rioters were burning down New York, or Detroit, the Hasan Pikers and El-Sayeds would be right there leading them and cheering them on.”
He continued: “What we saw in France – the hatred, the ingratitude, the desire to destroy rather than the desire to build – that exact same cancer is what has corrupted Abdul El-Sayed.”

Trump and his allies have sought to recast the demonstrations in France, which began as student protests against crumbling schools and the soaring cost of living , as evidence of the dangers of immigration and the erosion of western civilization.
Vance has made several visits to Michigan as Republican candidate Mike Rogers seeks to win the seat El-Sayed is vying for, launching a series of extreme attacks on the Democrat.

Trump, on a visit to the state on Sunday, accused El-Sayed of being “on the side of the terrorists” and said Michigan needed to “stand up and fight” against him. He has also repeatedly used his middle name, Mohamed.

El-Sayed told a rally of his own this weekend: “They think that by pointing at my name and my faith, that somehow you’re going to ignore the fact that you can’t afford your gas or your groceries, can’t see a doctor.”
Researchers have suggested this midterm elections campaign has seen the most concentrated wave of Islamophobic rhetoric in US electoral politics since the aftermath of 9/11.

“I really think everyone needs to pay attention to this cordinated [sic] campaign to delegitimatize Muslim Americans – not just as citizens but as humans,” Chris Murphy, the Democratic US senator for Connecticut, wrote on X on Tuesday morning.

Responding to recent remarks by Robert F Kennedy Jr, Trump’s health and human services secretary, who suggested “five hundred million Arabs in the world” do not contribute to science or literature, Murphy said: “These increasingly hysterical attacks are a prelude to Republicans bringing us to a very, very dark place after the election.”
body_zh: JD 万斯加大对民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的极端攻击| 2026 年美国中期选举
JD 万斯加大对民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的极端攻击力度
副总统试图将埃尔赛义德与巴黎抗议活动联系起来，并声称他将领导骚乱者“烧毁”底特律
JD万斯升级了对密歇根州美国参议院民主党候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德的煽动性攻击，他面临伊斯兰恐惧症的冲击，声称他将领导骚乱者“烧毁”底特律。
如果赢得下周的选举，埃尔赛义德将成为该国第一位穆斯林参议员，他被美国总统唐纳德·特朗普称为“圣战分子”。
副总统万斯已经指控埃尔赛义德是“可怕的邪恶”的代表，他为“一个群体而牺牲其他群体”而战，这促使埃尔赛义德回应说，剥夺人们的医疗保健和负担得起的食品杂货是“邪恶的”。
在周二的竞选活动中，万斯走得更远。
万斯在密歇根州豪厄尔向人群发表讲话，试图将埃尔赛义德的政治与巴黎的左翼抗议活动联系起来，这些抗议活动已导致数千人被捕。这位副总统描述了“成群结队的蒙面暴徒，其中许多人来自遥远的地方，占领了历史悠久的市中心”，同时还强调了赛义德与左翼政治评论员哈桑·皮克的关系。
“巴黎的破坏场景可能远在大洋之外，但扪心自问：在美利坚合众国这里真的很难想象吗？”万斯说道。 “我向你保证，如果那些暴徒烧毁了纽约或底特律，哈桑派克斯和埃尔赛义德就会在那里领导他们并为他们加油。”
他继续说：“我们在法国看到的——仇恨、忘恩负义、破坏的欲望而不是建设的欲望——正是同样的癌症腐蚀了阿卜杜勒·赛义德。”
特朗普和他的盟友试图将法国的示威活动重新定位为移民危险和西方文明侵蚀的证据，这些示威活动最初是学生抗议学校摇摇欲坠和生活成本飙升的抗议活动。
由于共和党候选人迈克·罗杰斯试图赢得埃尔-赛义德正在争夺的席位，万斯多次访问密歇根州，并对民主党发起了一系列极端攻击。
特朗普周日访问该州时指责埃尔赛义德“站在恐怖分子一边”，并表示密歇根州需要“站起来并与他作斗争”。他还多次使用他的中间名穆罕默德。
埃尔-赛义德在本周末的一次集会上说：“他们认为，通过指着我的名字和信仰，你会忽视这样一个事实：你买不起汽油或食品杂货，也看不到医生。”
研究人员表示，这次中期选举是自 9/11 事件以来美国选举政治中最集中的仇视伊斯兰言论浪潮。
康涅狄格州民主党参议员克里斯·墨菲 (Chris Murphy) 周二上午在 X 上写道：“我真的认为每个人都需要关注这场协调一致的运动，旨在使穆斯林美国人失去合法性——不仅是作为公民，而且是作为人类。”
特朗普的卫生与公共服务部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪(Robert F Kennedy Jr)最近表示，“世界上有五亿阿拉伯人”没有为科学或文学做出贡献，对此，墨菲回应说：“这些日益歇斯底里的攻击是共和党人在选举后将我们带入一个非常非常黑暗的境地的前奏。”

title_en: Trump campaigns in Mississippi, highlighting Republicans' challenges
title_zh: 特朗普在密西西比州的竞选活动凸显了共和党面临的挑战
summary: President Trump campaigned Monday in Mississippi, as he continued a closing midterm rally blitz that has highlighted Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统周一在密西西比州进行竞选活动，他继续进行最后一场中期集会闪电战，突显了共和党在大选前面临的挑战。
body_en: Trump campaigns in Mississippi President Trump campaigned Monday in Mississippi, as he continued a closing midterm rally blitz that has highlighted Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington.
Trump campaigns in Mississippi, highlighting Republicans' challenges
President Donald Trump arrives at a campaign rally at Crossroads Arena, in Corinth, Miss., Monday, Oct. 26, 2026. Jacquelyn Martin/AP hide caption

CORINTH, Miss. — President Donald Trump campaigned Monday in Mississippi, as he continued a closing midterm rally blitz that has highlighted Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington and statehouses across the country.
Republicans are spending millions and still may not win districts drawn to favor them

"I'm here because Cindy's doing great, but I just got to make sure. I can't take a chance," Trump told the crowd, his voice audibly hoarse, as he worked to boost Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, who is facing a surprisingly stiff challenge from Democrat Scott Colom.

Colom was spotted at the rally site, too, creating the rare spectacle of Trump's staunchest supporters interacting directly with a figure the president would soon go on to denigrate as a "Marxist radical" and "fake" and "shameless phony who pretends to be a moderate" from the stage.

Mississippi, among the nation's most reliably Republican states, is not where the Republicans envisioned needing a late-October stop from the president. But Colom is one of many Democratic underdogs who have managed to expand the House and Senate battleground maps because of widespread voter discontent over inflation, the Iran war and other aspects of Trump's second presidency.
He said he had planned to go to the rally site to listen to what was on Trump supporters' minds.
"They actually deserve a senator that will listen to them, that actually cares about what they think, actually cares about what they're going through," Colom said ahead of the president's arrival.

Trump's event kicks off a week of aggressive campaigning that will include more stops in states he won comfortably in 2024, including Texas, South Carolina and Iowa. Trump also plans to hold a rally Saturday in Salina, Kansas, officials announced late Monday, marking his second visit to the state in less than two weeks.
Former Vice President Kamala Harris speaks at Women for Crowley event Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in Milwaukee. Nam Y. Huh/AP hide caption
Democrats, including progressives, are expanding their efforts

Top Democratic candidates and their surrogates were also greeting voters — more than 30 million of whom have already cast ballots, according to data collected by The Associated Press from election administrators across the country — as they try to end Republicans' threadbare majority in the House, reclaim control of the Senate and claw back power in state capitals.

Former Vice President Kamala Harris, Democrats' 2024 presidential candidate, campaigned in Wisconsin with Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who faces Rep. Tom Tiffany, a Trump ally, in the governor's race. If elected, Crowley would be the first Black governor to lead the battleground state.
"This is a tight race because the stakes are so high," Harris said at an event billed as a "Women for Crowley" rally.
Meanwhile, in Michigan, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed distanced himself from an ad created by a group called Rebellion PAC that blames high grocery prices on U.S. support for Israel.

"This ad is not affiliated in any way with the Abdul for Senate campaign," a spokesperson for El-Sayed, Roxie Richner, said in a statement about the spot, which features a couple discussing U.S. support for Israel as they shop for groceries.
"Apparently it's costing us a lot of money to drop bombs on Gaza," the woman says.
The ad had been condemned by U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens, who narrowly lost to El-Sayed in the Democratic primary.
body_zh: 特朗普在密西西比州的竞选活动 特朗普总统周一在密西西比州进行竞选活动，他继续进行最后的中期集会闪电战，突显了共和党在可能彻底改变华盛顿权力的选举之前面临的挑战。
特朗普在密西西比州的竞选活动凸显了共和党面临的挑战
唐纳德·特朗普总统于 2026 年 10 月 26 日星期一抵达密西西比州科林斯十字路口竞技场举行的竞选集会。杰奎琳·马丁/美联社隐藏标题栏
密西西比州科林斯——唐纳德·特朗普总统周一在密西西比州进行竞选活动，他继续进行最后一场中期集会闪电战，突显了共和党在选举前面临的挑战，这场选举可能会彻底改变华盛顿和全国各州议会的权力。
共和党花费了数百万美元，但仍然可能无法赢得支持他们的选区
“我来这里是因为辛迪做得很好，但我必须确定一下。我不能冒险，”特朗普对人群说，他的声音明显沙哑，同时他正在努力支持共和党参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯，辛迪·海德·史密斯正面临着来自民主党人斯科特·科洛姆的令人惊讶的严峻挑战。
科洛姆也被发现出现在集会现场，创造了特朗普最坚定的支持者与总统直接互动的罕见奇观，总统很快就会在台上诋毁他是“马克思主义激进分子”、“虚伪”和“冒充温和派的无耻骗子”。
密西西比州是全国最可靠的共和党州之一，共和党人并不认为总统需要在 10 月底停下来。但由于选民对通货膨胀、伊朗战争和特朗普第二任总统的其他方面普遍不满，科洛姆是众多成功扩大众议院和参议院战场版图的民主党失败者之一。
他表示，他本来计划前往集会现场，听听特朗普支持者的想法。
“他们实际上应该有一位能够倾听他们的参议员，真正关心他们的想法，真正关心他们正在经历的事情，”科洛姆在总统到来之前说道。
特朗普的活动拉开了为期一周的积极竞选活动的序幕，其中包括在他于 2024 年轻松获胜的州进行更多站点，包括德克萨斯州、南卡罗来纳州和爱荷华州。官员周一晚间宣布，特朗普还计划周六在堪萨斯州萨利纳举行集会，这是他在不到两周内第二次访问该州。
前副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯 (Kamala Harris) 于 2026 年 10 月 26 日星期一在密尔沃基举行的女性支持克劳利活动上发表讲话。 Nam Y. Huh/美联社隐藏标题栏
包括进步人士在内的民主党人正在扩大努力
民主党的顶级候选人及其代理人也在向选民致意——根据美联社从全国各地选举管理人员收集的数据，其中超过 3000 万人已经投票——他们试图结束共和党在众议院的微弱多数，夺回对参议院的控制权，并夺回州首府的权力。
民主党 2024 年总统候选人、前副总统卡马拉·哈里斯 (Kamala Harris) 与密尔沃基县县长大卫·克劳利 (David Crowley) 在威斯康星州竞选，后者在州长竞选中面对特朗普盟友众议员汤姆·蒂凡尼 (Tom Tiffany)。如果当选，克劳利将成为第一位领导这个战场州的黑人州长。
哈里斯在一场名为“克劳利女性”集会的活动中表示：“这是一场紧张的竞选，因为赌注如此之高。”
与此同时，在密歇根州，民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德与一个名为 Rebellion PAC 的组织制作的广告保持了距离，该组织将高杂货价格归咎于美国对以色列的支持。
“这则广告与阿卜杜勒竞选参议院的竞选活动没有任何关系，”埃尔赛义德的发言人罗克西·里奇纳 (Roxie Richner) 在一份关于该广告的声明中表示，该广告的主角是一对夫妇在购买杂货时讨论美国对以色列的支持。
“显然，我们在加沙投掷炸弹花费了很多钱，”这位女士说。
该广告遭到美国众议员海莉·史蒂文斯的谴责，后者在民主党初选中以微弱优势输给了埃尔赛义德。

title_en: A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month
title_zh: 法官叫停了华盛顿特区高尔夫球场的翻修工程。特朗普称他们仍将在下个月开始
summary: A federal judge has barred the government from clearing more trees or making other alterations to D.C.'s East Potomac Park without proper notice. Trump says his administration will appeal.
summary_zh: 一名联邦法官禁止政府在没有适当通知的情况下清除更多树木或对华盛顿东波托马克公园进行其他改造。特鲁姆
body_en: A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month

President Trump, seen touring the East Potomac Golf Links in late June, says his administration will appeal the judge's ruling and close the course for renovations next month. Kent Nishimura/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

After weeks of tense hearings and late-night court filings, a federal judge has temporarily blocked the Trump administration from making any further alterations to East Potomac Park, the municipal D.C. golf course that the president wants to redevelop into a championship-level venue.

The long-simmering legal battle kicked into high gear in recent weeks, after the government cut down 430 trees on the golf course with less than a day's notice. That prompted a pair of lengthy court hearings that at times turned heated, with government officials repeatedly insisting that the tree-clearing was unrelated to the renovations President Trump had touted on social media. They contradicted the president's own social media posts from that very morning by saying there was no final plan for those renovations at all.

"Rarely, if ever, has the United States Department of Justice urged a federal court not to believe the sitting president," U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes wrote in her 70-page opinion . "And yet, here we are."
A D.C. park was made 'for the pleasure of the people.' Trump's plan would change that

Reyes extended what was initially a two-week halt to tree removal, ordering the government not to cut down "or substantially prune or otherwise damage or impair" any trees at East Potomac Park without a court order. She also ordered it to provide "no less than ten business days' written advance notice" before closing or making any "irreversible modification" to any parts of the park while the legal battle plays out.
"By issuing this preliminary injunction, the Court does not end the round: it simply marks the ball until the parties can fully and fairly litigate this case," Reyes wrote.

Monday's ruling is a win for the D.C. Preservation League and a pair of local golfers who sued to prevent renovations earlier this year — and for the growing grassroots movement to protect the municipal course and the surrounding recreational area, which is beloved by runners, cyclists, birders and others.

"We are grateful the court intervened to stop the Trump-Vance administration's greed and lawlessness while the case continues, and we are eager to argue the case in court," said Skye Perryman, the president of the nonprofit Democracy Forward, which is representing the plaintiffs.
Judge chastises Trump administration plan to push ahead overhaul of DC golf course
In a Truth Social post late Monday, Trump said the Department of the Interior will appeal the ruling. NPR has reached out to the Department of Interior but did not hear back in time for publication.

Trump also doubled down on his earlier announcement that construction will begin on Nov. 15 and keep the park closed for 15 months, adding that the "judge has absolutely no right to hold up this very important and beautiful Project."

"To have to give advanced notices to a judge who has no expertise in Golf, Architecture, Landscaping, Construction, or anything else having to do with building such a World Class Project, is not fair, appropriate, or Constitutional," Trump wrote.
Reyes herself has said she is not interested in policing the federal government's landscaping efforts.

That's why, as she explained in Monday's opinion, she repeatedly declined to intervene in the case — instead issuing repeated warnings against any unannounced major alterations — until "the Government did what it assured all it would not do."
"The Court earlier stated, 'I am not the Lorax. I do not speak for the trees,'" Reyes concluded. "The Court still does not speak for the trees. It speaks only for the rule of law."

On Tuesday afternoon, Reyes made a record of Trump's post and gave the government about 24 hours to clarify whether a plan exists to close East Potomac in mid-November and, if so, "how that can be reconciled" with what its lawyers previously told the court. She said she will schedule a status hearing for either Friday or Monday.
The judge took aim at the government's contradictions

Reyes' strongly-worded 70-page opinion came exactly a week after a seven-hour hearing in which she clashed repeatedly with the government's lawyers. She had already rejected the administration's request to recuse herself from the case because of alleged bias.
body_zh: 法官叫停了华盛顿特区高尔夫球场的翻修工程。特朗普称他们仍将在下个月开始
六月下旬，特朗普总统参观了东波托马克高尔夫球场，他表示，他的政府将对法官的裁决提出上诉，并在下个月关闭球场进行翻修。 Kent Nishimura/法新社来自盖蒂图片社 隐藏标题栏
经过数周紧张的听证会和深夜法庭文件后，一名联邦法官暂时阻止特朗普政府对东波托马克公园进行任何进一步改造，总统希望将东波托马克公园改造成锦标赛级场地。
最近几周，政府在不到一天的通知时间内砍伐了高尔夫球场上的 430 棵树，这场酝酿已久的法律战近几周进入白热化阶段。这引发了两次冗长的法庭听证会，听证会有时变得激烈，政府官员一再坚称砍伐树木与特朗普总统在社交媒体上吹捧的翻修工程无关。他们与总统当天早上在社交媒体上发布的帖子相矛盾，称根本没有这些翻修的最终计划。
美国地区法官安娜·雷耶斯 (Ana Reyes) 在长达 70 页的意见中写道：“美国司法部很少（如果有的话）敦促联邦法院不要相信现任总统。” “然而，我们到了。”
华盛顿公园是“为了人民的欢乐”而建造的。特朗普的计划将改变这一现状
雷耶斯延长了最初为期两周的树木清除禁令，命令政府在未经法院命令的情况下不得砍伐“或大幅修剪或以其他方式损坏或损害”东波托马克公园的任何树木。她还命令公园在法律诉讼期间关闭或对公园的任何部分进行任何“不可逆转的修改”之前提供“不少于十个工作日的书面提前通知”。
雷耶斯写道：“通过发布这一初步禁令，法院并没有结束这一轮比赛：它只是对球进行标记，直到双方能够充分、公平地对此案提起诉讼。”
周一的裁决对华盛顿特区保护联盟和两名当地高尔夫球手来说是一场胜利，他们今年早些时候提起诉讼，要求阻止翻修工程，对日益壮大的草根运动来说，这是一场胜利，以保护市政球场和周围的休闲区，这些休闲区深受跑步者、骑自行车者、观鸟者和其他人的喜爱。
代表原告的非营利组织“民主前进”主席斯凯·佩里曼表示：“我们很感激法院介入，制止了特朗普-万斯政府的贪婪和无法无天行为，同时案件还在继续，我们渴望在法庭上辩论此案。”
法官严厉谴责特朗普政府推动华盛顿特区高尔夫球场检修的计划
特朗普周一晚间在《真相社会》帖子中表示，内政部将对这一裁决提出上诉。 NPR 已联系内政部，但没有及时收到回复以供发布。
特朗普还强调了他早些时候宣布的施工将于 11 月 15 日开始并将公园关闭 15 个月的说法，并补充说“法官绝对没有权利阻止这个非常重要和美丽的项目。”
特朗普写道：“必须提前向一位在高尔夫、建筑、景观美化、施工或与建设这样一个世界级项目有关的其他领域没有专业知识的法官发出通知，这是不公平、不适当的，也不符合宪法。”
雷耶斯本人表示，她对监管联邦政府的景观美化工作不感兴趣。
这就是为什么，正如她在周一的意见中所解释的那样，她一再拒绝干预此案，而是反复警告不要进行任何未经宣布的重大变更，直到“政府做了它保证不会做的事情”。
“法院早些时候表示，‘我不是洛拉克斯人。我不代表树木发言，’”雷耶斯总结道。 “法院仍然不为树木说话。它只为法治说话。”
周二下午，雷耶斯记录了特朗普的帖子，并给了政府大约 24 小时的时间来澄清是否有计划在 11 月中旬关闭东波托马克，如果有，“如何与律师之前告诉法庭的内容相一致”。她说她将安排周五或周一举行状态听证会。
法官直指政府矛盾
雷耶斯在长达七小时的听证会一周后发表了措辞强硬的 70 页意见，听证会上她与政府律师多次发生冲突。她已经拒绝了政府因涉嫌偏见而回避此案的要求。

title_en: Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again
title_zh: 特朗普政府试图再次起诉前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米

body_en: Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again : NPR

Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute James Comey for what it calls a decade-old leak of classified information. Comey's lawyers immediately dismissed the effort as invalid and outside the time limit.
Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again
Former FBI Director James Comey speaks during a Senate Intelligence Committee hearing on Capitol Hill, Thursday, June 8, 2017, in Washington. Alex Brandon/AP hide caption

WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute James Comey for what it calls a decade-old leak of classified information, an effort the former FBI director's lawyers immediately dismissed as invalid and outside the legal time limit for when the Justice Department can file a criminal indictment.
Judge says DOJ illegally fired the daughter of former FBI director Comey
'8647' got James Comey indicted. What exactly does it mean?

The allegations from the Justice Department were revealed Monday in newly unsealed court documents that shed light on a closed-door fight that represents an unmistakable escalation in the administration's targeting of Comey, a longtime critic and foe of President Donald Trump who has faced two other criminal cases since the Republican returned to the White House last year. The effort to prosecute Comey is also part of a series of politically charged investigative actions the department has undertaken in the run-up to next week's midterm elections.

"Well, they're back — again," Comey said in a video statement Monday. "It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice – one that we cannot become numb to. Nothing's changed with me; I'm still innocent, I'm still not afraid of these people — and I still believe in an independent federal judiciary."
The Justice Department said it had filed what's known as a "criminal information" to extend the statute of limitations for when they can permissibly bring an indictment.

"Filing a criminal information to toll the statute of limitations is a widely recognized practice in federal court and has been approved by multiple Circuit Courts of Appeals. This is an ongoing criminal investigation, and we will not comment further," a department spokesperson said.

An information can be filed without the approval of a judge or a grand jury's finding of probable cause to a court. Comey's lawyers made clear that they intend to fight the charges as invalid and barred by a 10-year statute of limitations.
The case against Comey failed because of Trump's prosecutor. Who is she?
Grand jury indicts former FBI director James Comey for a second time

"For the third time in little more than one year, the Department of Justice has attempted to charge Mr. Comey with a federal crime. Mr. Comey steadfastly maintains his innocence," his attorney, Patrick Fitzgerald, said in a statement.

The latest allegation concerns an October 2016 New York Times story related to a secret court order that required Yahoo to scan emails for messages potentially linked to a foreign terrorist organization. The story cited two government officials who spoke on the condition of anonymity about the order from a judge on the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court that Yahoo was barred from publicly disclosing.

Federal authorities, including prosecutor John Durham, began investigating the disclosure in early 2017. Durham, who later investigated the FBI's conduct as it scrutinized potential ties between Russia and Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, wrote a classified memo in December 2018 recommending no criminal charges against anyone in connection with the disclosure, Comey's attorneys said in a recent court filing.

In January 2019, the U.S. Attorney's office for the District of Columbia opened a second investigation of the same matter under the code name "Tropical Vortex." But that investigation was closed without any charges filed in February 2020.

"Both times the Government determined that no charges should be brought against anyone. Now, ten years after the article was published, the Government filed an "Information" against Mr. Comey that was not approved by a judge nor issued by a grand jury. It purports to charge Mr. Comey with crimes that he did not commit," Fitzgerald said.

Prosecutors in a newly unsealed filing said investigators found evidence that Comey "sought to correct misinformation which had appeared in the press by way of Reuters the day before" that New York Times story was published, directed his staff to speak to a journalist at the newspaper related to accuracy concerns "and thereby illegally transferred classified information."
body_zh: 特朗普政府试图再次起诉前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米：NPR
特朗普政府试图再次起诉前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米 特朗普政府正试图起诉詹姆斯·科米，罪名是其所谓的长达十年之久的机密信息泄露事件。科米的律师立即驳回了这一努力，称其无效且超出了时限。
特朗普政府试图再次起诉前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米
前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米于 2017 年 6 月 8 日星期四在华盛顿国会山举行的参议院情报委员会听证会上发表讲话。亚历克斯·布兰登/美联社隐藏标题栏
华盛顿（美联社）——特朗普政府正试图以十年前泄露机密信息为由起诉詹姆斯·科米，这位前联邦调查局局长的律师立即驳回了这一努力，称其无效，而且超出了司法部提起刑事起诉的法定时限。
法官称司法部非法解雇前联邦调查局局长科米的女儿
“8647”让詹姆斯·科米被起诉。它到底是什么意思？
司法部的指控在周一新公布的法庭文件中披露，这些文件揭示了一场闭门斗争，这表明政府针对科米的攻击明显升级。科米是唐纳德·特朗普总统的长期批评者和敌人，自去年共和党重返白宫以来，科米还面临另外两起刑事案件。起诉科米的努力也是该部门在下周中期选举前夕采取的一系列政治调查行动的一部分。
“好吧，他们又回来了，”科米在周一的视频声明中说道。 “如果这不是司法部如此令人震惊的滥用行为，那几乎会很有趣——我们不能对此麻木不仁。我什么都没有改变；我仍然是无辜的，我仍然不怕这些人——而且我仍然相信独立的联邦司法机构。”
司法部表示，它已经提交了所谓的“犯罪信息”，以延长他们可以提出起诉的时效。
“提交犯罪信息以延长诉讼时效是联邦法院广泛认可的做法，并已得到多个巡回上诉法院的批准。这是一项正在进行的刑事调查，我们不会进一步发表评论，”部门发言人表示。
无需法官批准或大陪审团向法院调查可能的原因即可提交信息。科米的律师明确表示，他们打算对这些指控进行抗辩，认为这些指控无效，并有 10 年诉讼时效限制。
针对科米的案件因特朗普的检察官而失败。她是谁？
大陪审团第二次起诉前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米
“司法部在一年多的时间里第三次试图指控科米先生犯有联邦罪行。科米先生坚定地坚称自己无罪，”他的律师帕特里克·菲茨杰拉德在一份声明中表示。
最新指控涉及《纽约时报》2016 年 10 月的一篇报道，该报道涉及一项秘密法庭命令，该命令要求雅虎扫描电子邮件以查找可能与外国恐怖组织有关的消息。该报道援引了两名不愿透露姓名的政府官员的话说，他们谈到了外国情报监视法院一名法官下达的禁止雅虎公开披露的命令。
包括检察官约翰·达勒姆在内的联邦当局于 2017 年初开始调查这一披露。科米的律师在最近的一份法庭文件中称，达勒姆后来在审查俄罗斯与特朗普 2016 年总统竞选之间的潜在关系时对联邦调查局的行为进行了调查，并于 2018 年 12 月撰写了一份机密备忘录，建议不对与该披露有关的任何人提出刑事指控。
2019 年 1 月，美国哥伦比亚特区检察官办公室以“热带涡旋”为代号对同一事件展开第二次调查。但该调查于 2020 年 2 月结束，未提出任何指控。
“两次政府都决定不应对任何人提出指控。现在，在该文章发表十年后，政府向科米先生提交了一份“信息”，该信息未经法官批准，也未经大陪审团发布。它旨在指控科米先生犯下他没有犯下的罪行，”菲茨杰拉德说。
检察官在一份新公布的文件中表示，调查人员发现证据表明，《纽约时报》报道发表后，科米“试图纠正前一天通过路透社出现在媒体上的错误信息”，指示他的工作人员与该报的一名记者就准确性问题进行交谈，“从而非法传输机密信息”。

body_en: Federal agents search Beverly Hills mansion tied to ex-congressman Eric Swalwell
Home of wealthy developer Stephen Cloobeck searched in connection to sexual misconduct inquiry into Swalwell

Federal law enforcement agents searched a home in suburban Los Angeles early on Tuesday as part of an investigation into Eric Swalwell , who resigned from Congress amid a wave of sexual misconduct allegations, a law enforcement official and two people familiar with the investigation told the Associated Press.

Agents searched the Beverly Hills home of the wealthy developer and Swalwell donor Stephen Cloobeck, where the Democratic ex-congressman spent time before resigning from office in April, according to the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss the investigation.
Illinois man arrested after allegedly sending suspicious powder to Congress members using his return address
Messages seeking comment were left for Swalwell’s attorney and for a lawyer who represented Cloobeck in another matter.
Cloobeck, the founder of the Diamond Resorts International timeshare company, told the New York Post in April that he cut ties with Swalwell as accusations against him mounted.
“I am no longer associated with a man that takes advantage of women,” Cloobeck told the newspaper. “I support women’s rights.”

Tuesday’s search is the latest escalation in the federal investigation of Swalwell – one of several investigations begun after a woman came forward with allegations that he sexually assaulted her twice, including when she worked for him.

The San Francisco Chronicle, followed by CNN, first reported the allegations. CNN also reported that three other women alleged various kinds of sexual misconduct by Swalwell, including sending them unsolicited explicit messages or nude photos.

Asked about the search at Cloobeck’s address, an FBI spokesperson, Lourdes Arocho, said the bureau “early this morning … conducted an operation in the Los Angeles region related to an ongoing criminal investigation.
In August, federal agents seized electronic devices from Swalwell at the San Francisco airport and searched his Washington DC home.

Swalwell, an Iowa native, was elected in 2012 and represented a House district east of San Francisco. He launched a presidential run in April 2019 but ended it a few months later after failing to catch on with voters.
The seven-term lawmaker had been seen as one of the leading candidates in California’s gubernatorial race before dropping out after the allegations surfaced.

The office of the Manhattan district attorney, Alvin Bragg, has said it is also investigating Swalwell after a former staffer told CNN and the Chronicle that Swalwell raped her at a hotel while he was in New York City for a charity gala in 2024.
In a statement, Bragg’s office encouraged “survivors and anyone with knowledge of these allegations to contact” its special victims division.
Los Angeles prosecutors were also said to be weighing charges.

Swalwell was one of Donald Trump’s top antagonists in Congress. He was a prominent member of the House judiciary and intelligence committees during Trump’s first presidency and served as one of several Democratic prosecutors for Trump’s second impeachment after the 6 January 2021 attack on the US Capitol .

Swalwell was removed from the intelligence committee by the then US House speaker, Kevin McCarthy, a California Republican, in 2023 based on Swalwell’s contact with a suspected Chinese spy, Christine Fang.
Fang was reported to have come into contact with Swalwell’s campaign as he was first running for Congress in 2012 and to have participated in fundraising for his 2014 campaign.
body_zh: 联邦特工搜查与前国会议员埃里克·斯瓦尔韦尔有关的比佛利山庄豪宅
富有开发商史蒂芬·克鲁贝克 (Stephen Cloobeck) 的家因斯瓦尔韦尔性行为不当调查而被搜查
一名执法官员和两名知情人士告诉美联社，联邦执法人员周二早些时候搜查了洛杉矶郊区的一处住宅，作为对埃里克·斯瓦尔韦尔(Eric Swalwell)调查的一部分。埃里克·斯瓦尔韦尔因一系列不当性行为指控而从国会辞职。
据不愿透露姓名的知情人士透露，特工搜查了富有的开发商、斯瓦尔韦尔捐助者斯蒂芬·克鲁贝克 (Stephen Cloobeck) 在比佛利山庄的住所，这位民主党前国会议员在 4 月份辞职前曾在这里住过一段时间。
伊利诺伊州男子因涉嫌使用其回邮地址向国会议员发送可疑粉末而被捕
寻求评论的消息已留给斯瓦尔韦尔的律师和在另一件事中代表克鲁贝克的律师。
钻石度假村国际分时度假公司的创始人克鲁贝克四月份告诉《纽约邮报》，随着对斯瓦尔韦尔的指控越来越多，他与斯瓦尔韦尔断绝了关系。
“我不再与一个利用女性的男人有联系，”克鲁贝克告诉该报。 “我支持妇女权利。”
周二的搜查是对斯瓦尔韦尔的联邦调查的最新升级，这是在一名妇女站出来指控斯瓦尔韦尔对她进行性侵犯两次（包括在她为他工作时）之后开始的几项调查之一。
《旧金山纪事报》和美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 首先报道了这些指控。美国有线电视新闻网还报道称，另外三名女性指控斯瓦尔韦尔有各种不当性行为，包括向她们发送未经请求的露骨信息或裸照。
当被问及对克鲁贝克地址的搜查时，联邦调查局发言人卢尔德·阿罗乔表示，联邦调查局“今天凌晨……在洛杉矶地区开展了一项与正在进行的刑事调查相关的行动。”
八月，联邦特工在旧金山机场查获了斯瓦尔韦尔的电子设备，并搜查了他在华盛顿特区的家。
斯瓦尔韦尔是爱荷华州人，于 2012 年当选，代表旧金山以东的众议院选区。他于 2019 年 4 月发起总统竞选，但几个月后因未能赢得选民的青睐而结束。
这位七届议员曾被视为加州州长竞选的主要候选人之一，但在指控浮出水面后退出。
曼哈顿地区检察官阿尔文·布拉格办公室表示，正在调查斯瓦尔韦尔，此前一名前工作人员告诉 CNN 和《纪事报》，斯瓦尔韦尔 2024 年在纽约市参加慈善晚会时在一家酒店强奸了她。
在一份声明中，布拉格办公室鼓励“幸存者和任何了解这些指控的人联系”其特别受害者部门。
据称，洛杉矶检察官正在权衡指控。
斯瓦尔韦尔是唐纳德·特朗普在国会的头号对手之一。在特朗普第一任总统期间，他是众议院司法和情报委员会的重要成员，并在 2021 年 1 月 6 日美国国会大厦袭击事件后担任特朗普第二次弹劾的几名民主党检察官之一。
2023 年，由于斯瓦尔韦尔与中国间谍嫌疑人方芳 (Christine Fang) 的接触，时任美国众议院议长、加州共和党人凯文·麦卡锡 (Kevin McCarthy) 将斯瓦尔韦尔从情报委员会中除名。
据报道，方在斯瓦尔韦尔 2012 年首次竞选国会议员时就接触过他的竞选活动，并参与了 2014 年竞选活动的筹款活动。

title_zh: 特朗普任命的疾病预防控制中心副主任在上任六个月后辞职
summary: Jennifer Shuford is expected to leave her post after midterm elections ‘to spend more time with my family’ The deputy director and chief medical officer of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) will resign after six months on the job, according

body_en: Trump-appointed CDC deputy director to resign after six months on the job | Trump administration
Trump-appointed CDC deputy director to resign after six months on the job
Jennifer Shuford is expected to leave her post after midterm elections ‘to spend more time with my family’
The deputy director and chief medical officer of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) will resign after six months on the job, according to an agency email obtained by the Guardian.
Dr Jennifer Shuford was appointed by Donald Trump in April as part of a four-person senior leadership team.

The appointments were meant to stabilize the agency after the previous CDC director, Susan Monarez , left less than a month into the job – publicly describing the directives of the health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr , as “ unscientific ”.

“I am leaving to spend more time with my family,” Shuford said in a statement, sent via email by the CDC director, Dr Erica Schwartz. “I am so thankful to President Trump and Secretary Kennedy for giving me the opportunity to help lead CDC. It has been an amazing experience, and I will be forever grateful for it.”
Shuford is expected to leave her post on 12 November, after the midterm elections .

The deputy director was appointed as part of a four-person team in April, alongside Schwartz and two other top leaders. Shuford’s appointment was cheered by public health leaders, such as Association of State and Territorial Health Officials (ASTHO), who would have known her work as Texas health commissioner.
Trump described the team as “Highly Respected Doctors of Medicine [who] have the knowledge, experience, and TOP degrees to restore the GOLD STANDARD OF SCIENCE at the CDC”, in a social media post.

In the time since Shuford has worked at the agency, Kennedy has made significant changes that undermine vaccine trust and access. In just a few recent examples: Kennedy fired all 17 of the CDC’s expert vaccine advisory panel members and replaced them with ideologically aligned appointees, slow-walked death updates to the agency’s measles dashboard, and forced the CDC to publicly contradict scientific consensus on vaccines and autism – a change the Autism Science Foundation said left it “ appalled ”.

At the same time, the agency has lost one-third of its workforce and 48 distinct measles outbreaks have roiled the US, particularly in Pennsylvania . The overwhelming majority of Americans – including Maha supporters – trust vaccines.

“I am deeply grateful for Dr Shuford’s outstanding leadership and commitment to CDC and public health, especially as she has navigated an exceptionally demanding, high-profile, and constantly evolving environment over the past several months,” said Schwartz in the email announcing Shuford’s departure.
Dr Satish Pillai will serve as acting deputy director and chief medical officer as the team searches for a successor to Shuford.
body_zh: 特朗普任命的疾病预防控制中心副主任在上任六个月后辞职特朗普政府
特朗普任命的疾病预防控制中心副主任在上任六个月后辞职
詹妮弗·舒福德预计将在中期选举后离职，“以便有更多时间陪伴家人”
据《卫报》获得的一封机构电子邮件显示，美国疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）副主任兼首席医疗官将在上任六个月后辞职。
詹妮弗·舒福德博士于四月被唐纳德·特朗普任命为四人高级领导团队的一员。
这些任命旨在稳定该机构，此前疾病预防控制中心前任主任苏珊·莫纳雷斯（Susan Monarez）离职不到一个月，公开形容卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪（Robert F Kennedy Jr）的指令“不科学”。
疾病预防控制中心主任埃里卡·施瓦茨博士通过电子邮件发送的一份声明中，舒福德说：“我要离开，以便有更多时间陪伴家人。” “我非常感谢特朗普总统和肯尼迪国务卿给我机会帮助领导疾病预防控制中心。这是一次奇妙的经历，我将永远感激不尽。”
舒福德预计将于 11 月 12 日中期选举后离职。
副主任于四月被任命为四人团队的一员，与施瓦茨和其他两名高层领导一起。舒福德的任命受到了州和地区卫生官员协会 (ASTHO) 等公共卫生领导人的欢迎，他们对她担任德克萨斯州卫生专员的工作很了解。
特朗普在社交媒体帖子中将这个团队描述为“备受尊敬的医学博士，他们拥有恢复疾病预防控制中心科学黄金标准的知识、经验和顶尖学位”。
自从舒福德在该机构工作以来，肯尼迪做出了重大改变，破坏了疫苗的信任和获取。仅举最近的几个例子：肯尼迪解雇了 CDC 疫苗专家顾问小组的全部 17 名成员，并用意识形态上一致的任命者取而代之，在该机构的麻疹仪表板上缓慢更新死亡情况，并迫使 CDC 公开反驳有关疫苗和自闭症的科学共识——自闭症科学基金会表示，这一变化使其“感到震惊”。
与此同时，该机构失去了三分之一的员工，48 起不同的麻疹疫情席卷了美国，尤其是宾夕法尼亚州。绝大多数美国人——包括玛哈的支持者——相信疫苗。
施瓦茨在宣布舒福德离职的电子邮件中表示：“我非常感谢舒福德博士的杰出领导力以及对疾病预防控制中心和公共卫生的承诺，特别是在过去几个月里，她在一个要求极高、备受瞩目且不断变化的环境中度过了。”
Satish Pillai 博士将担任代理副主任兼首席医疗官，团队正在寻找 Shuford 的继任者。

title_en: Illinois man arrested after allegedly sending suspicious powder to Congress members using his return address
title_zh: 伊利诺伊州男子因涉嫌使用其回邮地址向国会议员发送可疑粉末而被捕
summary: Matthew Unglesbee admitted to sending the letters to four unidentified politicians, officials say An Illinois man accused of sending letters containing suspicious white powder to four members of Congress has been arrested after he allegedly wrote his own name
summary_zh: 官员称，马修·昂格尔斯比 (Matthew Unglesbee) 承认向四名身份不明的政客发送了这些信件。 一名伊利诺伊州男子被指控发送包含以下内容的信件
body_en: Illinois man arrested after allegedly sending suspicious powder to Congress members using his return address | US crime
Illinois man arrested after allegedly sending suspicious powder to Congress members using his return address
Matthew Unglesbee admitted to sending the letters to four unidentified politicians, officials say

An Illinois man accused of sending letters containing suspicious white powder to four members of Congress has been arrested after he allegedly wrote his own name and return address on the envelopes, according to authorities.
Matthew Unglesbee, 36, of Quincy, remained in the custody of US marshals on Tuesday on federal charges of perpetrating a hoax and sending threatening communications through the mail.

In an eight-page criminal complaint unsealed on Monday, Charis Hobbs – a taskforce agent with the FBI’s Springfield office – said Unglesbee admitted during an interview on Sunday that he sent the letters to the four unidentified politicians.

Unglesbee told the agent that the substance he placed inside the envelopes was salt – because it “kind of looks like” anthrax, the complaint said. Preliminary testing did not reveal the presence of any biological or chemical toxin.

“Each letter contained a white granular substance and a handwritten letter which read ‘ha ha’,” the court filing said. A letter to an unnamed US senator also contained granules and read “Hah enjoy the gift”.
On each of the four white, letter-sized envelopes, the agent said, Unglesbee wrote his name and home address in Quincy.

None of the staffers who handled the letters at any of the four Congress members’ offices in northern Illinois opened the envelopes, the complaint said. The offices had alerted each other to look out for mailings with Unglesbee’s name on them.

FBI personnel “trained in handling weapons of mass destruction, and threats of biochemical toxins” were sent to three of the politicians’ offices on Wednesday after staff called authorities, and hazardous materials (hazmat) response teams attended two of them.

Having retrieved the communications with Unglesbee’s address on them, FBI agents visited his home, where they discovered another envelope – empty and addressed, but not sent, to one of the same Congress member’s Washington DC office.

The suspect told investigators that he mailed four letters “after hearing someone in a restaurant mention the news story of other letters being sent”, the filing said. Earlier in October, the FBI and US Postal Inspection Service said they were investigating multiple reports of suspicious letters sent to state officials and election offices across the country.

Unglesbee denied participating in the other suspicious mailings. But he allegedly told investigators that he anticipated the Congress members would “take it serious” because the powder he sent could be perceived to be anthrax, which he said he knew was dangerous and would cause hazmat teams to have to respond.
“Unglesbee claimed he was joking but recognized the recipients would not know he was joking and could perceive it as a threat,” the complaint said.

In a justice department press release on Monday announcing Unglesbee’s arrest, Ryan Presley, special agent in charge of the FBI’s Springfield field office, said authorities were focused on “keeping our public institutions safe from intimidation”.

He said: “Mailing unknown substances to congressional offices creates fear and disrupts the public institutions vital to our democracy. We, along with our partners, will remain vigilant in identifying and holding accountable those whose actions threaten to intimidate public officials or disrupt our democratic systems.”
Unglesbee was tentatively scheduled to appear for a detention hearing on Wednesday afternoon in federal court in Springfield.

伊利诺伊州男子因涉嫌使用其回邮地址向国会议员发送可疑粉末而被捕
官员称，马修·昂格尔斯比承认向四名身份不明的政客发送了这些信件
据当局称，伊利诺伊州一名男子被指控向四名国会议员发送含有可疑白色粉末的信件，据称他在信封上写下了自己的名字和回信地址，因此被捕。
周二，36 岁的昆西人马修·昂格尔斯比 (Matthew Unglesbee) 仍被美国法警拘留，联邦指控他实施恶作剧并通过邮件发送威胁信息。
在周一启封的一份长达八页的刑事起诉书中，联邦调查局斯普林菲尔德办事处特遣部队特工查里斯·霍布斯 (Charis Hobbs) 表示，昂格尔斯比在周日接受采访时承认，他向四名身份不明的政客发送了这些信件。
诉状称，昂格尔斯比告诉特工，他放入信封内的物质是盐，因为它“看起来有点像”炭疽病。初步测试未发现任何生物或化学毒素的存在。
法庭文件称：“每封信都含有白色颗粒状物质和一封写着‘哈哈’的手写信。”一封写给一位未透露姓名的美国参议员的信中也含有颗粒，上面写着“哈，享受这份礼物”。
特工说，在四个信纸大小的白色信封的每一个上，昂格尔斯比都写下了他的名字和在昆西的家庭住址。
诉状称，在伊利诺伊州北部的四名国会议员办公室处理这些信件的工作人员都没有打开信封。各办公室互相提醒留意带有昂格尔斯比名字的邮件。
周三，在工作人员致电当局后，“接受过处理大规模杀伤性武器和生化毒素威胁培训的联邦调查局人员”被派往三间政客办公室，危险物质（危险物质）响应小组前往其中两间办公室。
在取回带有昂格尔斯比地址的通讯后，联邦调查局特工拜访了他的家，在那里他们发现了另一个信封——空的，有地址，但没有寄往同一位国会议员在华盛顿特区的办公室。
文件称，嫌疑人告诉调查人员，他“在一家餐馆里听到有人提及其他信件被发送的新闻报道后”寄出了四封信。十月初，联邦调查局和美国邮政检查局表示，他们正在调查多起向全国各地州官员和选举办公室发送可疑信件的报告。
Unglesbee 否认参与了其他可疑邮件。但据称他告诉调查人员，他预计国会议员会“认真对待”，因为他发送的粉末可能被认为是炭疽，他说他知道炭疽很危险，会导致危险品小组不得不做出反应。
诉状称：“Unglesbee 声称他在开玩笑，但他承认收件人不会知道他在开玩笑，并且可能会将其视为威胁。”
在司法部周一宣布逮捕昂格尔斯比的新闻稿中，负责联邦调查局斯普林菲尔德外地办事处的特工瑞安·普雷斯利表示，当局的重点是“确保我们的公共机构免受恐吓”。
他说：“向国会办公室邮寄未知物质会造成恐惧，扰乱对我们民主至关重要的公共机构。我们与我们的合作伙伴将保持警惕，识别那些威胁恐吓公职人员或扰乱我们民主制度的行为，并追究其责任。”
昂格尔斯比暂定于周三下午出席斯普林菲尔德联邦法院的拘留听证会。

Democrats have a midterm edge, poll shows. And, Israelis vote in high-stakes election
Democrats Lead In NPR Poll, Preparations For Election Challenge, Israel Voting Begins

A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll reveals that Democrats hold significant advantages in the midterm elections and are favored to gain control of the U.S. House. But there are also signs suggesting that a potential wave may be limited. The poll highlights key issues influencing voters ; one in three Americans face financial hardships, and four in 10 say their personal finances are worsening. Preserving democracy resonates with Democrats and independents, while immigration ranks as the top issue for MAGA supporters.

A member of the League of Women Voters of Greater Cleveland helps hold the flag during the national anthem before a basketball game on Oct. 26, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. Jason Miller/Getty Images hide caption

🎧 Democrats hold an 8-point advantage among likely voters on the generic congressional ballot, indicating a strong position, NPR's Domenico Montanaro tells Up First . President Trump remains unpopular. His approval rating sits at 40%, which is a slight improvement. While it seems unlikely that Democrats will lose the House, the Senate remains a toss-up . Montanaro says patience will be crucial for the outcomes of many races because it's unlikely the winners will be clear by election night, which is to be expected of vote counting in close elections.

➡️ The NPR App has all of NPR's election coverage in one place — from the biggest stories across the country, to the issues that matter close to home. Browse headlines, playlists, podcast episodes, videos and more, all on the 2026 Election tab .

A federal judge today hears arguments in the Trump administration's bid to compel California to set aside ballots from voters it alleges may not be citizens. This comes after an appeals court last night declined the administration's request to get involved.

🎧 Trump announced yesterday that he is offering a $1 million reward for tips on voter fraud that lead to a conviction. The president has claimed fraud in every election he has participated in, prompting Democrats, election officials and good-governance groups to prepare for similar accusations, NPR's Eric McDaniel says. The White House says its efforts aim to secure elections . But McDaniel says credible evidence of voter fraud significant enough to affect election outcomes in the U.S. has never been found.

➡️ With the elections a week away, Polymarket has already investigated "dozens" of bets on its prediction markets concerning the midterm elections, according to Shana Bautista, the company's head of global intelligence and investigations.

Israelis are voting today in an election that will shape their country's future. This marks the first time since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks that Israelis can choose their leaders. Voters will decide whether to keep Israel's far-right, longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, or replace him with Gadi Eisenkot , a former military chief promising more diplomacy and less extremism. Here's what you need to know about the leading candidates, the issues shaping the vote and what could happen next.

🎧 NPR's Ruth Sherlock says a high voter turnout is expected , and many people casting their votes believe this is a critical election for the country's future. Israelis abroad have flown in to participate. At a polling station, Sherlock met Itamar Ariel, who believes that only Netanyahu can ensure Israel's security, even though the country faces problems. Others in the country believe Netanyahu should be voted out due to security failures. Those wanting change in leadership want an investigation into how the Oct. 7 attacks in Israel happened, which Netanyahu has blocked. Sherlock says by Wednesday morning, we should see which side secures the most seats in Parliament , but the vote count could continue for days, and the prime minister won't be determined until after days or possibly weeks of negotiations between the parties.

Hours of screen time at your desk can turn you into a stiff, bleary-eyed version of yourself. Prolonged sitting can take a real toll, but a few smart habits can help reset your body and mind. Here are Life Kit 's best strategies to help with the discomfort and health risks that can come from sitting at a desk all day.
🧘 Walking for five minutes every 30 minutes helps combat fatigue, weight gain and joint pain, reducing the risk of chronic diseases like obesity, heart disease and cancer.
🧘 If your back aches from slouching at your desk, rotate your spine to relieve stress and enhance flexibility by mimicking its natural movements.
🧘 Fidgeting indicates a need to change your position. Pay attention to your body and switch between sitting, standing, reclining and moving.

🧘 To relieve eye strain from screen time, stretch your eye muscles. Hold your arm straight in front of you, thumb pointing up. Move your arm in a big circle while keeping your head still and follow your thumb with your eyes.
